title: Rigidity of automorphisms on pointed smooth curves of genus zero or one
statement: Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-field, def-weil-algebraic-closure], let $Y/k$ be a smooth projective connected curve [def-sc-curves, def-kun-projective], and let $b$ be a $k$-automorphism. Genus is [def-sc-genus], and $\operatorname{Pic}^0(Y)$ is the group of degree-zero invertible sheaf classes [def-sc-pic0, def-sc-invertible-module]. If $Y$ has genus zero, then $Y\simeq\mathbf P^1_k$, and if $b$ fixes three distinct $k$-points then $b=\operatorname{id}_Y$. If $Y$ has genus one and $b^*$ acts identically on $\operatorname{Pic}^0(Y)$, then for any choice of origin $O\in Y(k)$ the automorphism $b$ is a translation for the elliptic group law on $Y$ with identity $O$. Consequently, in genus one, identity on $\operatorname{Pic}^0(Y)$ together with one fixed $k$-point implies $b=\operatorname{id}_Y$.

proof.text: In genus zero apply [lem-trf-genus-zero-smooth-proper-line] to $Y$: its field is algebraically closed and it is smooth, proper and connected, with $g(Y)=0$. This gives a $k$-isomorphism $h:Y\simeq\mathbf P^1_k$. (Properness: the embedding of [def-kun-projective] is a closed immersion into $\mathbf P^N_k$, hence H-projective and quasi-compact, i.e. projective in the sense of [lem-pc-projective-proper], which makes $Y$ proper over $k$.)

source.place: Tag 0C6U, proposition-projective-line, algebraically closed genus-zero specialization.

proof.text: Conjugate $b$ by $h$. By [lem-sfb-projective-frames-pgl], with $S=\operatorname{Spec}k$ and $r=2$, this automorphism is induced by an invertible matrix $A$: a nonempty Zariski open of $\operatorname{Spec}k$ is all of it. Let $L_1,L_2,L_3$ be the three distinct fixed lines in the homogeneous coordinate space $k^2$. Choose nonzero $v_i\in L_i$ for $i=1,2$; they are a basis. Write a generator of $L_3$ as $a v_1+c v_2$, where $a,c\ne0$ since the three lines are distinct. Invariance of the first two lines gives $A v_i=\lambda_i v_i$. Invariance of the third gives $a\lambda_1=\mu a$ and $c\lambda_2=\mu c$, so $\lambda_1=\lambda_2$. Thus $A$ is scalar and its projective automorphism is the identity. Conjugating back gives $b=\operatorname{id}_Y$.

source.place: Lemma 1.15(c), printed p.85; agent expansion of the projectivity calculation, using the existing projective-automorphism node.

proof.text: Now suppose $g(Y)=1$ and fix an arbitrary $O\in Y(k)$. Apply [lem-sfb-genus-one-abel-group-identification] to this pointed curve. We obtain algebraic addition and inversion on $Y$, with identity $O$, and an additive bijection $\alpha=\alpha_O$, $\alpha(P)=[\mathcal O_Y(P-O)]$. In particular translation by every $k$-point is a $k$-scheme automorphism (its inverse is translation by the negative point).

source.place: Tag 0DSV, example-pos-dim, genus-one paragraph: the degree-one Abel map is an isomorphism and identifying Picard degree one with degree zero gives the abelian-variety structure.

proof.text: For the automorphism $b$, pullback of a divisor line bundle satisfies $b^*\mathcal O_Y(P-O)\simeq\mathcal O_Y(b^{-1}P-b^{-1}O)$. Here is the local check, rather than an extra functoriality assumption: the isomorphism of local rings induced by $b$ identifies a uniformizer at $P$ with a uniformizer at $b^{-1}P$, so preserves the normalized valuation. The valuation inequalities defining $\mathcal O_Y(D)$ in [def-sc-divisor] are therefore precisely the inequalities for $b^{-1}D$ after pullback [def-pc-module-pullback]. Applying the divisor-class homomorphism [lem-sc-divisor-class-curve] gives $b^*\alpha(P)=\alpha(b^{-1}P)-\alpha(b^{-1}O)$.

source.place: Tag 0DSV, example-pos-dim, Abel identification; agent local calculation for transport of divisor modules under an isomorphism.

proof.text: Put $c=b^{-1}(O)$. The assumption $b^*|_{\operatorname{Pic}^0(Y)}=1$ and step 4 give $\alpha(b^{-1}P)=\alpha(P)+\alpha(c)=\alpha(P+c)$ for every $P\in Y(k)$. Injectivity of $\alpha$ gives $b^{-1}P=P+c$. Replacing $P$ by $b(Q)$ gives $b(Q)=Q-c$. Taking $Q=O$ shows $b(O)=-c$, so $b(Q)=Q+b(O)$ on all $k$-points. No homomorphism property for $b$ has been assumed.

source.place: Tag 0DSV, example-pos-dim, genus-one paragraph: the degree-one Abel map is an isomorphism and identifying Picard degree one with degree zero gives the abelian-variety structure.

proof.text: The pointwise equality in step 5 is equality of scheme morphisms. To justify this explicitly, $Y$ is reduced by [lem-sc-smooth-regular]. For two $k$-morphisms $f,g:Y\to Y$ agreeing on $k$-points, the opens $f^{-1}V\cap g^{-1}V$, with $V$ affine in the separated target, contain every closed point: closed points are $k$-points by [lem-wf-affine-nullstellensatz-vanishing](1). They cover $Y$, since a nonempty closed complement in a finite-type scheme has a closed point (on an affine chart choose a maximal ideal of its nonzero quotient algebra and apply the same clause). On an affine open $U$ of one such intersection, for each $s\in\mathcal O(V)$ the section $f^*s-g^*s$ vanishes on all $k$-points of $U$. Clause (2) of that node makes it zero, since $U$ is reduced and of finite type. Thus the ring maps agree on every such chart, hence $f=g$. Apply this to $b$ and the algebraic translation $Q\mapsto Q+b(O)$. If $b$ has a fixed $k$-point $Q$, cancellation in $Q+b(O)=Q$ gives $b(O)=O$, and this translation is the identity. The origin was arbitrary.
